questions: Did this walking difficulty begin suddenly?
Did it begin after an injury, illness, or emotional stress?
Do you feel pain in your back, hips, or legs when walking?
Do either of your legs feel weak?
Do you have numbness or tingling in either leg?
Do you feel dizzy or as if the room is spinning?
Have you had fainting, loss of consciousness, or seizures?
Have you had trouble speaking, seeing, swallowing, or controlling one side of your body?
Have you lost control of your bladder or bowels?
Is your walking problem getting progressively worse?
Does your walking vary substantially from moment to moment?
Can you walk normally when you are alone or not concentrating on walking?
Can you stand still with your feet together without holding on?
Have you previously had a stroke, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson’s disease, neuropathy, or another neurologic condition?
Have you recently started or changed any medications, alcohol use, or recreational drugs?
Have you had similar episodes before?
Do you believe you might fall even when you are not actually losing your balance?
served: Simplified Functional Movement Disorders Rating Scale (S-FMDRS)
results: 1. genetic ataxia panel: 112 and 29 CTG repeats in ATXN8OS - confirms SCA8
2. brain MRI: cerebellar atrophy on sagittal T1 and axial FLAIR
3. Simplified Functional Movement Disorders Rating Scale (S-FMDRS): 3 - mild gait disturbance that normalises with distraction

ALTERNATIVE: Progressive cerebellar gait ataxia directly attributable to SCA8
